basis: Retinopathy, intellectual disability and deafness define syndrome; diabetes/hypogonadism occur in 80-99%. Common skin and skeletal abnormalities omitted by cap.
Skeletal muscle channelopathy causing myotonia; ocular, thyroid and swallowing manifestations are below 30%.
Absent pericardium and diaphragm define disease; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 30-79%.
Skeletal dysplasia, joint restriction, intellectual disability and hearing loss define syndrome; thickened fibrotic skin occurs in 19/21 patients.
Umbrella skeletal dysplasia characterized by bowed bones; no additional organ involvement established across subtypes.
Bacterial infection of the fauces/oropharynx, within the upper airway axis; systemic toxin complications are not established at 30%.
Woolly hair and hypotrichosis define the disorder; protruding ears and lip eversion are dysmorphic features without established functional injury.
Isolated inherited platelet disorder causing macrothrombocytopenia.
Acquired von Willebrand factor dysfunction causes bleeding; associated cardiac disease and neoplasms are underlying conditions, not organs damaged by this syndrome.
Nonsyndromic intellectual disability; ocular motor findings lack frequency evidence or demonstrated independent eye damage.
Localized suppurative infection associated with a tooth; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Immune-mediated peri-engraftment inflammation with defining pulmonary injury; transient rash and fever do not establish additional organ damage.
Congenital myopathy and urethral malformation define syndrome; hypospadias in 2/2. Respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle weakness rather than intrinsic lung disease.
Developmental delay is frequent (30-79%). Despite the broad description, cardiac defects, pigmentary changes, hearing loss and scoliosis are annotated at only 5-29%.
Spotted-fever rickettsiae infect vascular endothelium and cause small-vessel inflammation; transient rash does not establish lasting skin damage.
LH resistance impairs endocrine Leydig-cell function, causing hypergonadotropic hypogonadism.
The encephalitis parent and A92.31 identify neuroinvasive West Nile infection; the supplied definition also describes broader, often asymptomatic infection.
Metaphyseal skeletal dysplasia; dentition abnormalities are annotated in 30-79%, supporting dental involvement beyond skeletal disease.
Retinal dystrophy, obesity and digital malformations are core features; developmental delay 2/2 and intellectual disability 2/4. Renal insufficiency 1/3 omitted by cap.
Loss of normally mineralized bone mass defines disease; endocrine disorders causing secondary osteoporosis are separate underlying conditions.
Inherited macular/retinal degeneration with reduced visual acuity.
Autoimmune cutaneous dermatomyositis without clinical myopathy; interstitial lung disease affects roughly 30-50% in some cohorts, with substantial population variation.
Cerebral abnormalities and oculocutaneous hypopigmentation define syndrome; hearing loss 80-99%. Anemia and immune/neutrophil abnormalities omitted by cap.
Autoimmune thyroid inflammation causes postpartum thyroid hormone dysfunction; obstetric timing does not remove its endocrine and immune axes.
Immune-mediated lymphocytic inflammation of the pons and related CNS structures; perivascular enhancement does not establish systemic vascular disease.
